symptom: ako/mxcli#859 (rehearsal S3/S4-S7): re-running an identical script re-spliced a microflow on every run (`Modified microflow: X (spliced: 1 replaced)`, under mdl 0 too, drifting the layout +520px per run) when it named a member fully qualified: `sort by M.Dept.SortOrder`, `create M.Emp (M.Emp.Name = …, M.Emp_Dept = $d)`, `change $e (Emp_Dept = $d)`, `find $L by M.Emp_Dept = $d`. Under mdl 1 the phantom was refused inside a loop body ("the Loop changes inside its body"), beside an end event ("no free room for the fragment"), or merged with a neighbour into a fragment that declares/returns.
cause: diff-then-patch compares the declared statements with the parsed describe of the stored flow, and describe prints members in one spelling per construct (sort/create/find short, change associations in full), while the builder stores the same member for either spelling. The declared spelling was compared as written.
fix: describedMemberSpellings (flow_member_spelling.go), called in planFlowModify: a deep copy of the declared body with each member respelled the way describe prints it, only where resolveMemberChange / shortSortAttribute resolve both spellings to the same stored member (a same-named association of another module stays as written).
insight: An equality on describe output is only as good as the normalisation of the declared side: every spelling the builder accepts for one stored value is a phantom diff unless the comparison folds it. Normalise by resolving through the builder's own resolver and requiring the same result, not by string suffixes, or a real change of member compares equal. The loop/end-event/fragment refusals were all downstream of the one phantom — fix the diff, not each refusal.
